FINAL DIAGNOSIS: BREAST (LEFT), EXCISION: MALIGNANT SPINDLE CELL NEOPLASM, FAVOR SARCOMA, WITH RHABDOMYOSARCOMATOUS, CHONDROSARCOMATOUS AND MALIGNANT NERVE SHEATH DIFFERENTIATION, GRADE 2 0F 3, REMOVED_DATE CM IN GREATEST DIMENSION. SEE NOTES 1 AND 2. TUMOR IS <0.05 CM OF THE ANTERIOR, POSTERIOR AND SUPERIOR MARGINS NOTE 1: Rhabdomyoblasts and tumor cells with cytoplasmic cross-striations are identified, and minor foci of cartilaginous differentiation. Neither an invasive epithelial nor an in situ epithelial component are identified, and the tumor is entirely sampled for microscopic study. Using immunoperoxidase methods with several blocks, the following results were obtained: DESMIN majority of tumor cells positive MYOGENIN majority of tumor cells positive MYO- REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  majority of tumor cells positive  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID protein many tumor cells positive, in minor foci GFAP many tumor cells positive, in minor foci KERATIN, cocktail very rare isolated tumor cells positive KERATIN, 903 very rare isolated tumor cells positive KERATIN, wide spectrum very rare isolated tumor cells positive  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  negative  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  negative The findings are consistent with a sarcoma with several lines of differentiation. In other locations, the tumor might be categorized as a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor with heterologous (rhabdomyosarcomatous and chondrosarcomatous) differentiation. In the breast, however, an origin from an overgrown phyllodes tumor or metaplastic carcinoma cannot be excluded with certainty, although there is no evidence to support these latter two possibilities. The slides were also reviewed by Drs. Frederick Koerner, Melinda Lerwill, and Petur Nielsen, who concur in the interpretations being rendered. NOTE 2: The results of immunohistochemical staining for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and Her2/neu protein expression and of fluorescence in-situ hybridization studies for Her2/neu gene amplification will be reported in an addendum.
